scope: Named cornelian cherry (Cornus mas) cultivars grown for fruit, shippable to Annandale, NJ (zone 6b/7a; the species is hardy to zone 4). Unnamed seedlings and ornamental leaf-color forms (Variegata, Tricolor, Aurea, Golden Glory, Saffron Sentinel) are left out. US sellers mostly use trademark names for the Ukrainian cultivars (Pioneer = Lukianivskyi, Sunrise = Marina, Red Star = Vydubetskyi, Yellow = Yantarnyi), so the same tree shows up under both names. Plant two different cultivars for a good crop.

varieties.name: Elegant
varieties.summary: Heavy crops of dark red, pear-shaped fruit; sweet enough to eat fresh.
varieties.description: Ukrainian cultivar ‘Elehantnyi’, sold in the US as Elegant™. Bears heavy crops of glossy dark red, pear-shaped fruit that ripens late August into September and tends to hang on the tree rather than drop. Sweet enough for fresh eating when fully ripe, and good for preserves. Plant a second variety for best fruit set.

varieties.name: Pioneer
varieties.summary: Large, juicy, aromatic pear-shaped fruit that ripens about two weeks before Elegant.
varieties.description: Ukrainian cultivar ‘Lukianivskyi’ (Lukyanovskii), released in 1975 from Kyiv's botanical garden and sold in the US as Pioneer™. Very productive, with glossy dark red, pear-shaped fruit up to 1½" long; juicy, sweet and aromatic, and soft when fully ripe. Ripens late summer, ahead of Elegant.

varieties.name: Red Star
varieties.summary: One of the most productive cultivars; juicy, glossy dark red oval fruit.
varieties.description: Ukrainian cultivar ‘Vydubetskyi’ from Svitlana Klymenko's breeding work, released in 1990 and sold in the US as Red Star™. Among the heaviest croppers, with glossy dark red, oval fruit about 1¼" long and a sweet-tart, aromatic flavor. Needs another variety as a pollinizer.

varieties.name: Sunrise
varieties.summary: Rounded light red fruit streaked with orange; high sugar, tastes like the yellow types.
varieties.description: Ukrainian cultivar ‘Marina’, from Svitlana Klymenko's breeding work, sold by One Green World as Sunrise™. Rounded fruit with light red skin streaked orange; sweet, with a high sugar content and a flavor closer to the yellow-fruited varieties. Ripens early September.

varieties.name: Red Dawn
varieties.summary: Ukrainian red cultivar from the Kyiv breeding program, sold as Red Dawn™.
varieties.description: Ukrainian cultivar ‘Syretskyi’, from the Kyiv botanical garden program, sold in the US as Red Dawn™. A red-fruited selection often paired with Red Star or Sunrise to stretch the harvest.

varieties.name: Coral Blaze
varieties.summary: Bright coral-red fruit, among the sweetest; drops when fully ripe.
varieties.description: Ukrainian cultivar ‘Koralovyi Marka’, sold as Coral Blaze™. Larger and sweeter than average, with bright coral-red fruit (growers report around 12% sugar, among the highest). Fruit drops when completely ripe; 20–30 lb from a mature plant. Needs a pollinizer; Pioneer and Sunrise are suggested partners.

varieties.name: Exotica
varieties.summary: Ukrainian cultivar with large, sweet fruit (around 10% sugar reported).
varieties.description: Ukrainian cultivar ‘Ekzotychnyi’ (Ekzoticheskiy), sold in the US as Exotica™. Large red fruit with a relatively high sugar content for the species (growers report about 10%).

varieties.name: Svitlana
varieties.summary: Kyiv selection U-26, named for breeder Svitlana Klymenko.
varieties.description: Selection ‘U-26’ from the Kyiv breeding program, named Svitlana™ in honor of Dr. Svitlana Klymenko, who led Ukraine's Cornus mas breeding work for decades.

varieties.name: Yellow
varieties.summary: Amber-yellow fruit with a slightly tropical flavor; heavy cropper.
varieties.description: Ukrainian cultivar ‘Yantarnyi’ (“amber”), sold as Yellow™. One of the few yellow-fruited cornelian cherries: smaller fruit than the big reds, but growers report high yields and a tropical note to the flavor. Slow-growing.

varieties.name: Juliusz
varieties.summary: Polish cultivar bred at Arboretum Bolestraszyce.
varieties.description: Polish cultivar bred at Arboretum Bolestraszyce, one of Europe's main Cornus mas collections. Rarely offered in the US.

varieties.name: Ugolek
varieties.summary: Very dark, almost black-red fruit; name means “little ember”.
varieties.description: Eastern European selection whose name means “little ember”, for its very dark, almost black-red fruit. Rarely offered in the US.

varieties.summary: Eastern European selection; name means “firstborn”.
